See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. {"url": "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all%3Acomputational+models+of+identity+persistence+and+memory+continuity&max_results=4", "scope": "paper abstracts; preprints, peer-review status not verified", "excerpt": "title: Computing persistent Stiefel-Whitney classes of line bundles
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12543v3
published: 2020-05-26T06:56:58Z
summary: We propose a definition of persistent Stiefel-Whitney classes of vector bundle filtrations. It relies on seeing vector bundles as subsets of some Euclidean spaces. The usual Čech filtration of such a subset can be endowed with a vector bundle structure, that we call a Čech bundle filtration. We show that this construction is stable and consistent. When the dataset is a finite sample of a line bundle, we implement an effective algorithm to compute its persistent Stiefel-Whitney classes. In order to use simplicial approximation techniques in practice, we develop a notion of weak simplicial approximation. As a theoretical example, we give an in-depth study of the normal bundle of the circle, which reduces to understanding the persistent cohomology of the torus knot (1,2). We illustrate our method on several datasets inspired by image analysis.

title: Stabilizing the unstable output of persistent homology computations
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01700v5
published: 2015-12-05T20:42:33Z
summary: We propose a general technique for extracting a larger set of stable information from persistent homology computations than is currently done. The persistent homology algorithm is usually viewed as a procedure which starts with a filtered complex and ends with a persistence diagram. This procedure is stable (at least to certain types of perturbations of the input). This justifies the use of the diagram as a signature of the input, and the use of features derived from it in statistics and machine learning. However, these computations also produce other information of great interest to practitioners that is unfortunately unstable. For example, each point in the diagram corresponds to a simplex whose addition in the filtration results in the birth of the corresponding persistent homology class, but this correspondence is unstable.
